bull.b: Very high retention indicates that merchants are increasing their activity on dLocal rather than merely replacing churned volume. This deepening share of wallet can support durable payment-volume growth, improve customer economics, and strengthen relationships across the company’s global merchant base.

bull.t: Strong volume growth and raised outlook
bull.b: Exceptional TPV growth, combined with a higher full-year outlook, shows strong demand for dLocal’s cross-border payment infrastructure. Sustained volume expansion can increase transaction-fee revenue and operating scale, while the guidance raise signals continued management confidence in execution.

Minimal leverage reduces interest, refinancing, and solvency pressure, giving dLocal flexibility to invest in product expansion or absorb volatility in emerging markets. Strong returns on equity also indicate that the company has been generating substantial earnings from its capital base.

bear.b: The decline in gross and net margins suggests that earlier profitability levels have not been fully sustained as the business has scaled. Continued compression would reduce the earnings benefit of strong payment growth and could limit reinvestment capacity if pricing or processing costs remain unfavorable.

Lower take rates can prevent transaction growth from translating proportionally into revenue and gross profit. The mix shift toward lower-priced flows and large-merchant pricing tiers therefore creates an ongoing risk to monetization, even if payment volumes continue expanding rapidly.

The recent rebound in cash generation is encouraging, but the prior negative year demonstrates that conversion from earnings to cash can fluctuate materially. Such volatility may complicate capital planning and makes durable cash generation less predictable than the latest TTM figures imply.
